subject: Coordinated purge cadence — telemetry retention carve-in & rollback clause
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia@mediq.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@mediq.com>, Eli Tsu <eli.tsu@mediq.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention carve-in for telemetry logs / purge timing

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — MediQ's security team had a follow-up ask about telemetry and log retention specifically. Our regulators require a short-term retention carve-in for raw telemetry (7 days) but they also want a documented rollback/escrow plan if a purge accidentally deletes evidence needed for an investigation.

Two asks: could Redwood provide a proposed purge cadence (including a short holding window for telemetry), and language we can include in the DPA appendix describing the rollback/escrow process?

Appreciate a tight turnaround — procurement would like something by end of next week.

Best,
Olivia Park
MediQ — Head of Security Programs

[Attachment referenced: mediq_evidence_req_2026.pdf]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@mediq.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Eli Tsu <eli.tsu@mediq.com>, Procurement Team <procure@mediq.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention carve-in for telemetry logs / purge timing

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear ask and the attach. We can do this. High level response below and I'll loop in ops/legal details.

Proposed (initial):
- Raw telemetry (debug-level logs, request traces) retained for 7 days by default for your account.
- After day 7, an automated staggered purge begins in 24h batches across shard groups; full purge completes by day 9.
- We will maintain immutable snapshots of telemetry metadata (hash + pointers) for 30 days to support investigation rollbacks. Snapshots are lightweight but sufficient to locate and rehydrate data from backups if needed.

Rollback/escrow approach (draft):
- On validated request (security incident or regulatory order), Redwood will initiate a retention rollback workflow: freeze purge, escalate to on-call ops, and trigger a targeted restore from the most recent backup snapshot (aim: restore to investigation node within 48 hours).
- If rehydration is required beyond standard backups (e.g., archived cold storage), Redwood will coordinate retrieval under a documented SLA (target 5 business days).

I'm attaching a short OPS csv with the staggered purge timeline and a DPA appendix draft for your legal team to review. Jordan/Tessa: can you validate the restore SLAs below and confirm any operational caveats?

Thanks — I'll aim to update this doc after your notes.

Kimberly Park
Senior Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: rwinference_dpa_appendix_telemetry_carvein_v1.pdf, proposed-purge-schedule-ops.csv

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-02T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention carve-in for telemetry logs / purge timing

Kimberly / Olivia — quick ops confirmation and a few technical caveats.

Confirmed:
- 7-day raw telemetry retention then 48–72 hour staggered purge window is feasible for a Dedicated/Private customer like MediQ.
- Immutable metadata snapshots for 30 days is fine; they will include per-request ID, timestamp, model variant, and storage pointer. Snapshots are encrypted and KMS-wrapped per account.

Caveats / limitations:
- Point-in-time rehydration to a specific request may fail if data has been compacted and deduplicated across shard boundaries; we can mitigate by keeping raw chunks for 30 days only for high-sensitivity accounts (cost impact).
- Restore SLA: 48 hours for warm backups (recent snapshot). Cold-archive retrieval is 3–7 business days depending on region and subprocessor transfer times. We should call out both in the appendix.

Operational ask: MediQ must provide a named incident lead and validation evidence before we begin a rollback rehydration. This prevents spurious restores and aligns with our security controls.

Jordan Blake
Director, Serving Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@mediq.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention carve-in for telemetry logs / purge timing

Thanks Jordan — adding the rollback clause and a short checklist for incident validation (legal/ops steps):

Rollback checklist (draft):
1) MediQ submits formal request via security@redwood.com with incident ID and signed validation form.
2) Redwood security reviews evidence within 4 business hours and logs an incident ticket.
3) Ops freeze purge pipelines for affected shards and snapshot current state.
4) Targeted restore executed to a customer-isolated workspace for MediQ investigators.
5) Post-restore: joint RCA and purge-gap analysis to improve future guardrails.

Price/limits note: we recommend keeping the paid warm-chunk hedge for 30 days if MediQ wants guaranteed point-in-time rehydration; otherwise the 30-day snapshot+cold-archive path is best-effort for cost efficiency.

I'll fold this into the DPA appendix language Kimberly attached and return next iteration.

Tessa Morgan
Sr. Product Manager, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Eli Tsu <eli.tsu@mediq.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T14:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention carve-in for telemetry logs / purge timing

Kimberly, Jordan, Tessa — thanks for the fast turn. A few legal asks from our side after internal review:

1) We need the appendix to include the exact notification timeline Redwood will provide before an irreversible purge (48 hours notice to our security inbox).
2) Clarify the point about immutable metadata — MediQ requires the snapshot hash plus provenance chain be exportable for third-party auditors.
3) For the escrow/rollback SLA: can Redwood commit to a maximum 5 business day cold-archive retrieval window for US-region accounts and include a credit clause if the SLA is missed (e.g., pro-rated service credit)?

We are okay with the incident validation step, but request a contact roster for on-call ops and an out-of-band verification phone number.

Would you take these items into the next draft appendix? Procurement is preparing a PO but wants the appendix resolved first.

—Eli
Legal Counsel, MediQ

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@mediq.com>, Eli Tsu <eli.tsu@mediq.com>, Procure Team <procure@mediq.com>

Date: 2026-10-06T17:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention carve-in for telemetry logs / purge timing — updated appendix

All — attaching updated DPA appendix that incorporates the notice window, exportable snapshot provenance, and a cold-archive SLA with a small credit mechanism (see section 4.3).

Short answers inline:
- 48-hour irreversible purge notification: yes, Redwood will send an automated alert + ack request to MediQ's security inbox; purge will not proceed until ack is recorded or the 48-hour window elapses.
- Snapshot export: we will provide an exportable compressed provenance bundle (hash chain + signed manifest) for audit requests—subject to standard egress fees if over 1GB.
- Cold-archive SLA: committed 5 business days for US-region retrieval; if missed we will issue a pro-rated service credit capped at one month of telemetry service fees.
- On-call roster and an out-of-band number: Jordan will share the ops roster (private doc link) and we will provide a 24/7 verification phone number to your security contacts.

Next steps: I'll drop the updated PDF into the Drive folder and route a DocuSign envelope for the appendix amendment. If you want a quick thumb-up meeting, Jordan and I can carve 30 minutes tomorrow morning.

Thanks — Kim
Senior Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
